Select the penalty parameter along an L1 path

Source: R/selection.R
mc_select_lambda.Rd

Builds a geometric grid of penalty values down from the smallest value that zeroes every edge, \(\lambda_{\max}=n\max_{i<j}|\hat S_{e,ij}|\), to lambda_min_ratio times that value. At each grid point the penalized model of mc_graph_penalized is fitted, its support is refitted without penalization, and the information criterion is evaluated on that refit. The selected penalty is $$\hat\lambda=\arg\min_{\lambda}\ \mathrm{crit}\bigl(\hat{\mathcal G}_\lambda\bigr),$$ with \(\hat{\mathcal G}_\lambda\) the support of the penalized solution at \(\lambda\); ties go to the larger penalty. The grid starts at \(\max(\lambda_{\max},10^{-3})\): the lower limit keeps the geometric grid defined when the residual covariances are numerically zero, and it does not change the first solution, which is the empty graph at any penalty of at least \(\lambda_{\max}\).

Usage

mc_select_lambda(
  fit,
  n_lambda = 30L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 0.001,
  criterion = c("bic", "aic", "qic", "gbic", "clbic", "ebic"),
  refit = TRUE,
  workers = 1L,
  warm_start = FALSE,
  include_zero = FALSE,
  ebic_gamma = 0.5,
  cluster = NULL,
  small_sample = FALSE,
  max_iter = 300L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  kkt_tol = 1e-04
)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph" (GGM layer).

n_lambda

number of grid points (default 30).

lambda_min_ratio

ratio of the smallest to the largest penalty (default \(10^{-3}\)).

criterion

"bic" (default), "aic", "qic", "gbic" or its alias "clbic", or "ebic".

refit

logical; if TRUE (default) the returned fit is the unpenalized refit of the selected support. If FALSE, the penalized solution is attached to the fit instead; its covariance is kept for diagnostics but it is flagged as not certified for edge-wise inference.

workers

number of parallel workers for the penalty grid. The grid points are independent fits, so the selected penalty does not depend on this value. Sequential by default; see mc_graph_stability for why it is opt-in. Not used with warm_start = TRUE.

warm_start

logical; run the grid in sequence from the largest penalty, each fit starting at the previous solution.

include_zero

logical; add the unpenalized complete graph as the candidate at \(\lambda=0\).

ebic_gamma

the parameter of the extended BIC, used only with criterion = "ebic".

cluster

optional independent-cluster identifier, one per residual row, passed to mc_compute_criterion: Pearson contributions are summed within clusters in QIC and GBIC, and the number of clusters replaces the number of rows in the logarithmic penalty of BIC, GBIC and EBIC.

small_sample

logical; apply the cluster factor \(G/(G-1)\), with \(G\) the number of clusters, to the empirical variability of the clustered criteria (default FALSE); ignored without cluster.

max_iter, tol, kkt_tol

passed to mc_graph_penalized at every grid point.

Value

An object of class "mcg_selection" (see mc_graph_stepwise for the common components) with method = "penalized", the selected lambda, a logical warm_start, and the table lambda_path, a data frame with one row per grid point (plus one for \(\lambda=0\) when include_zero = TRUE) and columns lambda, n_edges, criterion, penalized_converged, penalized_status, refit_converged and refit_status.

Independent fits, warm starts and the unpenalized end

By default every grid point is an independent fit from the same starting value, the diagonal fit \(\eta_{kk}=1/\widehat S_{e,kk}\), which also gives the largest penalty of the path; both need \(\widehat S_{e,kk}>0\) for every response, and a response whose Pearson residuals have no variance is refused with an error. The points can be evaluated in any order and with any number of workers, and the selected penalty does not depend on either. With warm_start = TRUE the grid is run from the largest penalty down, each fit starting at the solution of the one before, which is the usual way of computing a path; the fits are then sequential and workers is not used. The problem has a unique solution, so the two routes share the target and differ in the number of iterations. Certified solutions satisfy the optimality conditions only up to the tolerance, so their supports can differ in pairs whose zero-edge optimality condition, the scaled gap between the residual covariance and the fitted covariance, is close to \(\lambda\), within a margin proportional to the tolerance and to the conditioning of the curvature. With include_zero = TRUE the unpenalized fit of the complete graph is added to the candidates as the end of the path, \(\lambda=0\); the geometric grid never reaches it. By default the grid is independent and does not include that end.

Which grid points compete

The criterion is evaluated on the unpenalized refit of the support of every grid point whose penalized fit was certified, by the parameter change and by the KKT residual, and whose refit converged. A point without the certificate stays in lambda_path with its status and does not enter the comparison. An error is raised when no grid point qualifies.

See also

mc_graph_penalized, mc_compute_criterion.

Other structure selection: mc_edge_scores(), mc_graph_penalized(), mc_graph_stability(), mc_graph_stepwise()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 300; x <- rnorm(n)
y1 <- rnorm(n); y2 <- 0.6 * y1 + rnorm(n); y3 <- rnorm(n)
d <- data.frame(y1 = y1, y2 = y2, y3 = y3, x = x)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1 ~ x, y2 ~ x, y3 ~ x), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
sel <- mc_select_lambda(f, n_lambda = 10)
sel$edges
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    2
sel$lambda_path[, c("lambda", "n_edges", "criterion", "penalized_status")]
#>         lambda n_edges criterion penalized_status
#> 1  156.2001035       0  2565.181        converged
#> 2   72.5016656       1  2474.515        converged
#> 3   33.6522922       1  2474.515        converged
#> 4   15.6200104       1  2474.515        converged
#> 5    7.2501666       3  2484.557        converged

#> 8    0.7250167       3  2484.557        converged
